answer: A verifiable delay function deters Sybil attacks by binding each agent identity to an unbroken cryptographic thread of sequential computations. To participate, an agent must solve continuous time-lock puzzles, whether deployed in an orchard or on a terrace. An adversary incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of dedicated wall-clock processor time and electricity per identity. However, this imposes coordination latency and favors adversaries equipped with faster, specialized hardware.
